mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects a restrictive monetary policy environment that increases the cost of capital and reduces corporate earnings growth potential.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no significant correlation with 20-day returns (Spearman rank correlation < 0.1) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The condition (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) occurs in more than 20% of the time periods, but the 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in those periods.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of restrictive monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year) creates a 'stagflation' risk that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (FEDFUNDS>4.5% AND CPIAUCSL>2.5%) occurs in more than 20% of the time periods, but the 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in those periods.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to adopt an accommodative monetary policy, which leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate rate cuts and economic stimulus.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.0%, the 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates improving consumer confidence and economic activity, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST level shows no significant correlation with 5-day returns (Spearman rank correlation < 0.1) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 110.0) signals a weakening economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 110.0, the 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST > 1700.0) and retail sales (RSAFS > 360000.0) indicates strong consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (HOUST>1700 AND RSAFS>360000) occurs in more than 20% of the time periods, but the 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in those periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals a tight labor market, which is associated with rising inflation and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.0%, the 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.
